- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., 75+), overshooting by 2–5% in the following 3–5 days; apply dampening factor.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 75→70→69), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast slope in 3–5 day horizon.  
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns negative within 5 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% per day.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles, model tends to misalign with trend direction; align forecast with sentiment’s dominant recent polarity.
